findings.description: `premiseProblems` calls `own` and `inSiblings`, but neither identifier is defined, so the first premise raises an error instead of producing a readiness verdict. Any ticket naming a checkable file, script, path or function reaches this loop through `checkTicket`, and the factory cannot process its readiness result.
findings.title: Tickets with premises cannot be checked

evidence.explanation: `premiseProblems` creates holdings but invokes two undeclared identifiers inside its loop; `checkTicket` calls that loop before it can return problems to the factory.

findings.description: `checkTicket` passes `refresh` as a fifth argument to `premiseProblems`, whose signature accepts only four arguments and has no sibling-refresh callback. This fails TypeScript checking; if run without typechecking, a premise absent from the ticket repo is checked against a sibling's potentially old `origin/main` instead of its current revision.
findings.title: Checks cannot refresh sibling repos

evidence.explanation: The call supplies a fifth argument, while the callee declares four parameters and reads sibling holdings without invoking a refresh. The added test expects a needed sibling's refresh failure to propagate.

findings.description: `sourceTexts` decodes Git’s batch output as a JavaScript string but uses Git’s byte-sized blob length to slice it and locate the next header. If one source file contains enough multibyte text to move the offset past the next header’s SHA, later source files are skipped, so an existing helper in one of them is reported as a stale premise.
findings.title: Unicode-heavy source blocks valid tickets

evidence.explanation: `cat-file --batch` supplies a byte size, while `encoding: "utf8"` makes `batch` a string. For example, 21 em dashes add 42 bytes of disparity against UTF-16 string offsets: after the first blob, the parser starts within the next header’s `blob` field, obtains an invalid size, and stops reading subsequent files. Function holdings then come solely from the incomplete `sourceNames` result.

findings.description: `checkTicket` calls `refresh` on every existing sibling checkout before determining whether the ticket has any premises to check. If an unrelated sibling’s remote is unavailable, even a ticket with no backtick tokens throws during readiness; the factory leaves that ticket eligible and picks it again on subsequent ticks.
findings.title: An unused sibling can halt ticket checks

evidence.explanation: The refresh loop runs before `premisesOf`, and `refreshRef` throws on a failed fetch. The factory calls readiness before setting `claimed`; its failure handler therefore does not relabel the ticket, while the next tick selects the oldest eligible ticket again.

location.code_snippet:
+  // Read today's main, not the last fetch: a run builds from what origin holds now.
+  for (const dir of [checkout, ...siblings]) refresh(dir);

findings.description: `premiseProblems` reads the checkout’s current `origin/main`, but the factory refreshes that ref only after `checkTicket` finishes. If main changes between the checkout’s last fetch and workspace creation, readiness can approve a premise absent from the agent’s worktree or reject one that the worktree would contain.
findings.title: Tickets can be checked against old main

citations.citation:
/** The revision every premise is checked against: what a fresh run checks out. */
export const MAIN_REF = "origin/main";
// The agent works from this exact text, taken after the claim, so nothing added later can steer it.

evidence.explanation: The new lookup defaults to `origin/main`. The factory checks readiness before calling `workspace`, while `workspace` fetches main and creates the worktree afterward, so the two steps can observe different commits.

findings.description: `sourceNames` greps and parses individual lines, so it loses names inside multiline named imports. A ticket naming the existing `renameSync()` import, for example, is reported as stale; the factory then removes its ready label instead of starting the run.
findings.title: Valid imported helpers block ticket runs

  appendFileSync,
  copyFileSync,
  existsSync,
  mkdirSync,
  readdirSync,
  readFileSync,
  renameSync,
  rmSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from "node:fs";
renameSync(file, graveyard);

evidence.explanation: The grep pattern selects the line starting with `import`, but `renameSync` appears on a later line of that declaration and is called in the same source file. The per-line parser cannot recover the omitted name, and the factory treats a resulting problem as not ready.

findings.description: `checkTicket` resolves `factory.json` paths to the current working trees rather than the `origin/main` revisions used by the factory workspace. On a local branch with an unmerged helper or file, the premise passes even though the agent's fresh worktree will not contain it; local deletions can also reject a valid ticket.
findings.title: Local runs can approve stale tickets

evidence.explanation: The new resolver passes local directories to premise lookups, whereas the factory creates its agent worktrees from `origin/main` only after readiness succeeds.

findings.description: `premiseProblems` builds each problem as `stale premise: <token> (<kind>) not found` and never includes the checkout or sibling locations that were searched. A maintainer reading the factory's readiness report therefore cannot tell whether a missing file was searched for in this repo only or also in the sibling checkouts, which the rule requires to be reported.
findings.title: Stale reports omit the lookup location

citations.citation: Check ticket premises against the main checkout

evidence.explanation: The rule requires each missing item to report its name and lookup location. The message at line 155 carries only the token and kind, so the lookup location is absent from every stale-premise line.

findings.description: `classify` skips only paths beginning literally with `private/`, despite accepting a leading `./` in path tokens. A ticket naming `./private/config/snapshot.json` is consequently checked as a repository path and reported stale when private storage is absent from the checkout.
findings.title: Private paths can falsely stop tickets

evidence.explanation: `PATH` accepts an optional leading dot, but the exclusion tests only the unnormalized string for a `private/` prefix; path lookups then report missing files.

location.code_snippet:
+  const path = text.replace(/:\d+(?:-\d+)?$/, "");
+  if (PATH.test(path)) return path.startsWith("private/") ? null : { token: path, kind: "path" };

findings.description: `classify` rejects whitespace in an `npm run` token before `NPM_RUN` can extract its script name. A ticket that writes `npm run test:integration -- --runInBand` in backticks therefore yields no script premise, even when `test:integration` is absent from `package.json`.
findings.title: Script commands with arguments go unchecked

evidence.explanation: The whitespace test runs on everything following the optional `npm run` prefix, while the next line's npm parser only needs the initial script name.

findings.description: `allFiles` uses `statSync` and recursively enters directory symlinks without detecting cycles. When a ticket names a bare file or function and its checkout contains a link back to an ancestor, the inventory recurses until it fails; links outside the checkout can also make external files count as premises.
findings.title: A checkout link can stall readiness

evidence.explanation: Both bare-file and function lookups invoke `allFiles`; `statSync` follows symlinks, and the recursive walk has neither a cycle guard nor a checkout boundary.

findings.description: `exportedNames` scans every `.ts`, `.mts`, `.js` and `.mjs` file in the checkout, and accepts `export let` and `export async function` as well. A ticket naming a helper that is exported from outside `packages/harness/src/` and `.claude/hooks/` therefore passes, although the checklist says it must be reported as stale.
findings.title: Helpers exported elsewhere pass the gate

citations.citation: Check ticket premises against the main checkout

evidence.explanation: The rule requires functions be checked against `export function` or `export const` declarations in `packages/harness/src/` and `.claude/hooks/`. Lines 98-101 search the whole checkout and accept more export forms, so a missing function is accepted when a file outside those directories exports it.

findings.description: `PATH` accepts `..` components and `holdings` checks the resulting token without verifying that it stays inside the checkout. A ticket containing `../outside.ts` can therefore pass because a file beside the repository exists, although that file is not in the checkout being validated.
findings.title: Parent files can pass checkout checks

evidence.explanation: The path expression permits `../outside.ts`, and the path lookup joins it directly to the checkout before calling `existsSync`. The command exposes a readiness result rather than file contents, so the demonstrated impact is an incorrect existence check.

findings.description: `checkTicket` now throws when the selected checkout is absent, but the factory calls it before assigning `claimed` or changing the ticket's ready label. On a local run without the configured target sibling clone, the outer error handler leaves that ticket eligible, so subsequent ticks can pick it again instead of reaching younger tickets.
findings.title: A missing clone can block the ticket queue

findings.description: `proseOf` removes only fences beginning at column zero and `<details>` tags with no attributes. Indented Markdown fences or an `<details open>` block in a ticket's Notes remain available to `premisesOf`, so backticked paths in those examples can wrongly stop the ticket.
findings.title: Some examples become stale premises

citations.citation: A prior ticket-readiness bug came from treating fenced Markdown content as real ticket structure.

evidence.explanation: The first replacement is anchored at column zero, the second requires literal `<details>`, and unremoved text is subsequently searched for backtick tokens. An earlier accepted fix in this parser area likewise excluded fenced headings before interpreting ticket prose.

findings.description: `premisesOf` skips the first required section and checklist, and its 80-character introduction heuristic drops backtick tokens even when a preceding verb such as `adds` describes something else. As a result, ticket-named paths, scripts, and functions go unchecked, including a missing helper in a Done-when item or an existing file mentioned after a separate creation clause.
findings.title: Deliverable premises escape the check

citations.citation: Extract ticket premise references from eligible text

/** Words that announce something the ticket will create, read from the sentence before the token. */
const INTRODUCES = /\b(?:new|creates?|created|adds?|added|gains?|introduces?|introduced|writes?)\b[^`.]*$/i;

evidence.explanation: The extraction rule covers all sections except code blocks and Original wording details, but lines 67–68 skip whole deliverable sections and line 71 skips tokens using a keyword heuristic. The `INTRODUCES` regex can match `adds` anywhere before a token up to a period or backtick, so a semicolon and “reuse the existing” do not stop `premisesOf` from omitting `src/helpers.ts` in “The change adds telemetry; reuse the existing `src/helpers.ts`.” The PR describes these skips as deliberate narrowings, but both exclude eligible references.

findings.description: `premiseProblems` treats a premise as satisfied when any configured sibling checkout contains the path, without checking whether the ticket names that sibling. When a faultforge ticket refers to a file missing from its own repo but present in a sibling, the factory proceeds as though the file exists in the ticket’s repo without reporting the stale premise.
findings.title: Sibling repos hide missing premises

citations.citation: Check ticket premises against the main checkout

evidence.explanation: `checkTicket` supplies every other configured repo as a sibling, and `premiseProblems` uses `holders.some` to accept a match in any of them without retaining which repo the ticket named. As a result, a path absent from the ticket’s checkout can be counted as present because it exists in an unrelated sibling.
